prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks

statement.case_for: B038 remains my preferred achievement. The magic-wavelength lattice-clock idea solved a fundamental limitation of neutral-atom clocks, and its experimental development has made time and frequency measurement an unusually clean probe of gravitation and fundamental physics. Katori and Ye represent complementary and readily intelligible contributions: the defining concept and its decisive realization at exceptional precision. Most importantly, the result is no longer a single impressive apparatus: independently developed clocks have repeatedly demonstrated the underlying physics and its extraordinary performance.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that optical lattice clocks sit within the longer history of atomic frequency standards and optical metrology. The citation must honor the distinct lattice-clock breakthrough, rather than appearing to recognize all optical-clock development. Some of the most dramatic prospective applications and fundamental discoveries are still unfolding, so the case rests primarily on the completed conceptual and experimental advance.

responses.point: Kroll emphasizes that independent clock systems now operate reproducibly at extraordinary accuracy, while noting that their ultimate scientific consequences remain under development.
responses.response: I agree with this balance. Reproducibility across laboratories is especially important here: it shows that the advance is a robust physical method, not merely an engineering record. A completed prize-worthy advance need not wait for every application, provided the new measurement regime itself is securely established.

responses.point: Johansson ranks trapped-ion quantum computation and simulation highly, while warning that this broad quantum-information history intersects with earlier recognition of ion-trap quantum control.
responses.response: B030 is a serious alternative because its theory-to-experiment path is clear and experimentally mature. I nevertheless retain B038 above it: the lattice-clock achievement has a more sharply delimited central invention and attribution, whereas distinguishing the proposed quantum-information achievement from previously recognized ion-trap control requires a more difficult boundary judgment.

responses.point: Olsson argues that high-gain X-ray free-electron lasers have created a transformative ultrafast, atomic-scale probe, but stresses the distributed credit among theory, accelerator physics, and facility teams.
responses.response: I share the assessment of the scientific power of B008 and keep it as an alternative. Its attribution problem is nevertheless material: a prize limited to three names would need a much more exact historical account of the relation between high-gain FEL theory and large-scale realization than B038 requires.

uncertainties: How narrowly the historical development of the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept can be separated from the wider optical-frequency-metrology community.
Whether the committee considers the demonstrated measurement regime sufficient without awaiting a uniquely decisive fundamental-physics discovery enabled by these clocks.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
